message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Two relevant developments were reported during the last 24 hours: a Redis advisory update indicating observed exploitation of CVE-2026-25243, and a new NHS England alert covering three NGINX memory-safety vulnerabilities. No new MongoDB-family finding was confirmed.

**Scope:** `Products.txt` and `List_of_SIA_Completed.txt` only, combined, normalized, and deduplicated. `DLL_software_component.txt` was not read or combined.

**Scan window:** 2026-10-18 23:40 UTC through 2026-10-19 23:40 UTC (2026-10-19 05:10 IST through 2026-10-20 05:10 IST).

### Finding 1: Redis CVE-2026-25243 exploitation update

- **Affected product/component:** Redis Software and Redis OSS/Community Edition
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-25243, invalid memory access in the `RESTORE` command
- **Severity:** High, CVSS 7.7 (Redis)
- **Description:** An authenticated user allowed to run `RESTORE` can submit a crafted serialized payload that may cause invalid memory access and remote code execution. On October 19, the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security updated its advisory to state that open-source reporting indicates exploitation in the wild.
- **Why relevant:** Redis is explicitly present in the monitored product list.
- **Sources:** [Canadian Centre for Cyber Security update](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/alerts-advisories/redis-security-advisory-av26-423); [Redis vendor advisory](https://redis.io/blog/security-advisory-cve202623479-cve202625243-cve-2026-25588-cve202625589-cve-2026-23631/)

### Finding 2: NGINX CVE-2026-15176, CVE-2026-93479, and CVE-2026-97205

- **Affected product/component:** NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus
- **Issues:** Heap buffer overflows involving `alias`/`rewrite` and regex-based `map` processing; use-after-free when asynchronous file I/O and SSI are used
- **Severity:** CVSS v4 9.2 each in the F5/NHS alert; nginx.org categorizes the three issues as medium
- **Description:** Under affected configurations, crafted unauthenticated HTTP requests may crash worker processes and cause denial of service; code execution may be possible when ASLR is disabled or bypassed. NGINX Open Source 1.31.7 and stable 1.30.6 are listed as not vulnerable.
- **Why relevant:** Nginx is explicitly present in the monitored product list. The consolidated NHS alert was published October 19; the vendor fixes were released October 14.
- **Sources:** [NHS England cyber alert](https://digital.nhs.uk/cyber-alerts/2026/cc-4872); [NGINX security advisories](https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html)

### Possible matches needing review

None.

### MongoDB ecosystem verification

The dedicated sweep checked MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, `mongod`, `mongos`, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, `mongosh`, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, official drivers and connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, official integrations and maintained libraries, MongoDB-owned alerts, CVE records, GitHub Security Advisories, and CISA/government sources. No credible MongoDB-family vulnerability was newly reported or materially updated during the scan window; older entries were excluded.

### Review priority

Immediate review is recommended. Prioritize Redis deployments because exploitation has now been reported, then identify NGINX instances and configurations affected by the three highlighted CVEs and compare deployed versions with the vendor's fixed releases.
